title: Down to Earth
year_note: Released November 1986; it climbed slowly and spent three weeks at 3 in February 1987.

notes.made: Stewart Levine, who had produced Simply Red's Picture Book, the Crusaders and Hugh Masekela, was brought in to rescue the debut after sessions with Sly & Robbie, Paul Staveley O'Duffy and Culture Club's Roy Hay were abandoned. He produced six of the album's tracks, this one included. The band (Ben Volpeliere-Pierrot, Julian Brookhouse, Nick Thorp and Migi Drummond) wrote it with session keyboard player Toby Andersen, who co-wrote ten songs and was let go three months after the album came out.
notes.context: 'Misfit', the first single, had stiffed in August 1986 despite a video with Andy Warhol in it. Mercury wanted to hold the next single until after Christmas; the band insisted on November, and it crept up the chart for three months. In April 1987 Keep Your Distance went in at number 1. Smash Hits called the singer 'Ben Vol-au-vent Parrot', and his beret was really a fisherman's cap worn back to front.

listen_for.note: A light baritone, as one retrospective put it, kept cool over a rhythm section that knows where the one is.

leads_to.title: Grazing in the Grass
leads_to.why: Stewart Levine produced it, a US number 1, eighteen years before he took on a band of South-West London lads in hats.

notes.unverified: I couldn't find session players, horn credits or any description of this track's arrangement, so there is only one listen note, and it describes the band generally. Desmond's 'UK #3' is right.

culture.title: Three weeks at 3
culture.line: Mercury wanted to wait until after Christmas; the band insisted on November 1986, and the single climbed until it spent three weeks at 3 in February 1987.

culture.title: Straight in at number 1
culture.line: Keep Your Distance entered the UK album chart at number 1 in April 1987 and stayed in the top ten for 13 weeks.
